The 16 favourites were originally priced at $150–$180; seven remain available from the Drunk Beaver Rocks Webstore. The ranking leads with Olbia Super-Klone, (Boba) FET OverBooster, Trainer TS-15 MKII, Inglorious Bastard V3 and Bloom V2, followed by Khelnytskyi OD, Kyiv Lead, Mykolaiv, Forest Song, Kavun, Vatra, Mariupol, Hostomel, Lutsk, Kherson and Okhtyrka. Across them are evolved Klon, FET, Traynor, Blues Breaker, Expandora, OD-1, SD-2, Magnetic Saturation, Screamer, MOSFET, Jazz Chorus, Tube Driver, Tweed 5E3, SD-1 and Honey Bee designs. In the wake of the quite superb recent Olbia Super-Klone - which is my favourite Drunk Beaver Overdrive to-date as well as by far and away my favourite evolved Klon sound. I thought I should do a roundup / overview of my other favourite Drunk Beaver Overdrives too. This listing and visual is roughly in order of my preferences - where fortunately - the first 5 pedals listed are mostly on general release. Vitalii has made 26 Overdrives so far by my count. Actually there’s a couple of earlier editions that I missed out on - the T-Rex Custom Tube Bender with Mod, and the Alpaca Drive take on the Red Llama. Vitalii is considering re-issuing those at some stage - so I might end up at full completion in the end! All of Vitalii’s takes are enhanced and evolved from the original source material - sometimes significantly so. While even the simplest of these has some highly unique aspects for their overall makeup and output texture! So 17 of the 26 were pedal drops, with the remainder being Mainstream / General Release editions - I ended up somewhat serendipitously with half-and-half General Releases and Pedal Drops in my rundown of 16. I thought it best to draw a line somewhere - while I could have included a few more - there’s only a tiny number of Drunk Beaver Overdrives that I didn’t gel with ... yet! As mentioned - these are listed largely in order of preference - while the later selections become a little more nebulous on relative positions. - **Identity basis:** Contemporary exact-model coverage identifies Drunk Beaver's Forest Song as a high-voltage overdrive with resonant EQ and multiple clipping modes. The archive retains its existing catalog name.

The **Drunk Beaver Forest Song** is a high-voltage overdrive built around a nonstandard resonant EQ section and multiple selectable clipping options. Contemporary coverage identifies the 2024 release as the **Forest Song High Voltage Overdrive**, with a control set of **Volume, Resonance, Drive, and Mode**. [1][2]

The distinctive **Resonance** control is described as two peak-filter centers, approximately **500 Hz and 800 Hz**, with cut/boost behavior. The **Mode** control selects among several clipping approaches. Contemporary coverage lists **Boost, LED, MOSFET, Silicon, Germanium, and Asymmetric Silicon** options and reports operating voltages around **18 V and 30 V** for the high-voltage architecture. [1][2]

Guitar Pedal X describes the 2024 production release as the **third major iteration**, while noting an earlier V1 prototype. The same coverage says the earlier prototype's Germanium mode was weaker and the later production version refined the clipping implementation. [1]

This evidence supports a development history with multiple iterations, but it does not establish a complete factory revision numbering system. The archive therefore records the reported V1/prototype and V3 production history without inventing intermediate revision details.

The high-voltage architecture and multiple clipping modes are well documented in contemporary coverage. The reviewed sources do not provide a complete factory schematic or universal component BOM, so the archive does not assert individual semiconductor part numbers or claim that every surviving unit has identical component values.
